title: Finite refinements and local lifting
statement:
For a quasi-compact quasi-separated $X$, split etale hypercovers finite in
each degree [def-weil-pbc-finite-split-hypercover] exist. Their homotopy
category is cofiltered. A finite collection of local lifting requirements on
their terms in finitely many degrees can be satisfied after refinement,
provided each requirement is locally solvable for the etale topology.
Consequently an arbitrary etale hypercover can, through any specified finite
degree, be refined by one finite in each degree.

proof.text: Existence follows from the finite split existence construction. A finite split hypercover has the ordinary hypercover condition by its stored matching witnesses. The product of two such hypercovers is a hypercover. Its all-degree finite split replacement maps to both factors by composition with the product projections. For parallel maps take the ordinary endpoint-path homotopy equalizer hypercover, replace it by a finite split one, and precompose its elementary homotopy; this gives an EqvGen relation.

source.place: Lemmas 01GI (lemma-product-hypercoverings) and 01GS (lemma-homotopy), proof with the endpoint mapping object, using Lemma 01GN (lemma-add-simplices); Lemma 094K for the finite split replacement

proof.text: For each degree n define S_n as the intersection, over the finite set of pairs (j, theta:[degree(j)] to [n]), of the pullback of R_j along U(theta). Finite intersections of covering sieves are covering. A composite operator theta followed by alpha is another index of this intersection, so functoriality of U proves stability of S under every simplicial operator. This includes all the degeneracies that can affect a retained local requirement.

Take a finite replacement stage in degree zero solving S_0. Apply the constrained successor-stage theorem recursively; dependent choice gives a compatible tower whose stages all solve S. Assemble this tower retaining its finite solving cofans. In the prescribed degree of R_j, membership in S includes the identity operator, hence the constituent composite belongs to R_j. Substituting the equality degree(j)=n removes the transport in the stated conclusion. This constructs the required refinement and finite cofan in every retained degree, including the empty requirement family and empty cofans.

Convert the semi-representable hypercover to the ordinary étale hypercover condition using the singleton matching-object comparison, then apply the finite split replacement theorem. Truncating the resulting simplicial map gives the required map through degree r.

source.place: Lemma 01GJ (lemma-covering), statement and relative-cover construction; Lemma 0DAV, split extension; Lemma 094K, finiteness of each degree
